item.title: Why Williams breached the 2025 F1 cost cap
item.description: Motorsport photo Williams' breach of Formula 1's cost cap regulations for the 2025 season was down to a difference in interpretation between its own finance team and the FIA adjudicators, relating to the company's restructure as the team moved assets into a new limited liability partnership. The Grove squad was found to have committed a "minor overspend breach" of £627,000 in the 2025 cost cap, although the FIA conceded that this was unintentional given its interpretation of the costs involved. Williams subsequently accepted the breach, which comes with a 1.5% penalty to its aerodynamic testing allowance, and an undisclosed fine. According to team principal James Vowles, Williams believed that a company restructure would count as a financial and legal activity, both of which are classed as exemptions under the 2025 cost cap regulations. The FIA did not agree. "We've gone back through it exactly now and what should we have done differently. And clearly, we should have done something differently as a result of it," Vowles stated. "And although the regulations aren't clear in black and white in its interpretation, the FIA is very clear on their perspective, which is the following: because you've moved contracts from one business to the next, that effectively for them is procurement, which is an included activity. "For us, we defined it as a financial and legal activity because it's literally taking a contract and changing a name on it. I can understand their interpretation, which is why we've accepted the breach. Alexander Albon, Williams Alexander Albon, Williams "But I hope that helps you understand why it's subtleties, not clarity, really, in that circumstance." As seen from its logs on Companies House, the scenario is that Williams - having traded as Williams Grand Prix Engineering Ltd since 1977 - had set up a new LLP: Williams Grand Prix Engineering Services LLP, and moved £27.8m worth of assets and liabilities into the new company. WGPE Ltd is the 99% partner in the LLP, with BCE GP LLC - a holding company understood to be managed by Dorilton Capital - registered as the 1% minority partner. By doing this, WGPE Ltd has a degree of legal separation in place and, for example, will usually not be liable for any debts accrued by the LLP. Vowles says that this is about ensuring a degree of future-proofing for the team, and another in a long line of expenses involved in bringing Williams up to date. As such, the majority of the £627,000 overspend has been tied up in incorporating the new LLP, and in transferring any legal documents and supply contracts to the new company. item.title: A closer look at Deportivo A Coruna’s Barcelona DNA ahead of La Liga clash
item.description: A closer look at Deportivo A Coruna’s Barcelona DNA ahead of La Liga clash Barcelona will look to maintain their winning run as they take on Deportivo A Coruna this weekend. The Catalans are leading the La Liga table by three points and cannot afford any mishap. However, they will be coming up against a Deportivo side that is more than capable of springing a surprise. Heading into this clash, Hidalgo has already heaped praise on Barcelona while talking about his Barça past, having started his journey at the Catalan club. Deportivo’s Barcelona DNA Hidalgo started his journey at Barcelona. (Photo by Jose Manuel Alvarez Rey/Getty Images) As reported by Mundo Deportivo , Deportivo A Coruna have deep connection to Barcelona, which runs far deeper than their head coach alone. Hidalgo was a member of the famed “Quinta del Troya” generation, joining the Barça academy as a youngster, where he struck up a close friendship with Xavi Hernandez. When Xavi later took charge of the first team, Hidalgo was even a candidate to lead Barça Atletic before he eventually joined Deportivo. After guiding Deportivo back to the top-flight at the first attempt, Hidalgo has built a reputation as a coach capable of reviving clubs under pressure. But he is far from the only member of his staff with Blaugrana roots. Oscar Hernandez’s remarkable eye for talent One of Hidalgo’s assistants is Oscar Hernandez, who spent more than a decade at La Masia and comes with a superb scouting pedigree. It was Hernandez who, alongside Isidre Gil, authored the very first report on Lamine Yamal, back when the Spaniard was turning out for La Torreta . The forward agreed to a trial and the rest, as they say, is history. Hernandez also played a key role in recruiting Take Kubo before continuing his own career abroad. He served as an assistant to Javier Mascherano with the Argentina national team and now oversees Deportivo’s day-to-day training sessions. A squad packed with ex-Barcelona stars Aubameyang is set to face Barcelona this weekend. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) Apart from the coaches, Deportivo as a team is full of players with a Barcelona past. Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang is by far the biggest name, as is Marc Casado, who is on loan at the club until the end of the season. There are others such as Adama Traore, Arnau Comas, Adria Altimira and Luismi Cruz, all having passed through the club at various points. All of it sets the stage for an interesting clash this weekend, as Barcelona look to maintain their lead at the top of the table.

item.title: Jalen Brunson reveals why he prefers Stephen Curry over Magic Johnson as ‘GOAT’ NBA point guard
item.description: Credit: Joy Malone/Stephen Lam/San Francisco Chronicle via Getty Images In a discussion about the greatest point guard to ever play in the NBA, Jalen Brunson broke down why he chooses Stephen Curry over Magic Johnson. Having won Finals MVP while bringing an NBA title to the New York Knicks, Jalen Brunson has firmly put himself in the conversation as one of the all-time great point guards to play the game. However, that is a long list, and one that has some truly incredible names at the top. When talking about the GOAT NBA point guard, the conversation largely boils down to two names, Stephen Curry and Magic Johnson. Magic was instrumental in ‘saving the NBA’, and won five championships with the Los Angeles Lakers. Curry revolutionised the game with his shooting, and has four championships to his name. Brunson recently shared why Steph edges Johnson out on his list. Jalen Brunson says he personally prefers Stephen Curry’s shooting over Magic Johnson’s passing The Warriors superstar and the Lakers legend are completely different players. While Curry is a decent passer and has a dribbling package, his greatest strength has been his off-ball movement and three-point shooting. Magic was known for using his size and incredible court vision to unlock the offence, taking over the scoring only when necessary. When Brunson was talking about the GOAT PG debate with Dave Burd on the Roommates Show, he made his preference clear while breaking it down. “Totally different players. Me? I’m picking Steph Curry. I’m sorry,” Brunson said. “I got to have the person you have to guard when he steps on the court, no matter where he is on the court. That threat, where he just might be open, is scary for defenders. But then you have Magic Johnson who can make any pass or start any break. I prefer the shooting.” Brunson clearly explained his logic in picking Curry, and while many fans may disagree, the Knicks star seems certain of his opinion. Picking between Steph and Magic would be difficult for absolutely any basketball fan, but at least now fans know what the reigning Finals MVP thinks. item.title: “I’m So Worried”: Erin Andrews Fears Hearing Loss Due to Loud NFL Stadiums During FOX Sideline Coverage
item.description: Copyright: xJavierxRojasx ©IMAGO/ZUMA Press Wire Working on the sidelines for FOX Sports’ broadcast crew comes with front-row access to the biggest games in the NFL. One can even converse alongside play-by-play voice Kevin Burkhardt and seven-time Super Bowl champion Tom Brady. But behind the polished live hits and seamless communication with the broadcast booth, veteran sideline reporters, including Erin Andrews, need to withstand the loud fans in the stadium. Being just a few feet away from 70,000 excited fans every Sunday could be an occupational hazard. But there’s a device to counter that. During the recent episode of Calm Down With Erin And Charissa , Charissa Thompson asked Erin Andrews to talk about the interruptible foldback (IFB) that the broadcasters use while covering the games live to minimize the crowd’s noise. But Andrews’ response revealed a lesser-known fear. “So, we have these things called IFBs in our ears,” Andrews said. “They’re like full molds. Mine are because I’m so worried about hearing loss. And for my first hit, in our ears, in our IFBs, we get program. That’s what I get, so I can hear Kevin [Burkhardt] and Tom [Brady]. And then also, can get in my ears are my director, my producer, and some of the guys in the truck as well. So, I can talk to Casey, I can talk to GC about timing or about graphics or about any sort of stats.” During commercial breaks, Andrews confirmed that she could ask the technical team to turn her microphone up so she could talk to Burkhardt and Brady. The conversation could vary, but the threat is real. The health risks facing sideline reporters are rarely discussed. Subscribe to stay informed on the behind-the-scenes challenges shaping NFL coverage. “And then usually for the game, I take one ear out so I can hear what’s happening with the players, the coaches, the fans,” Andrews continued. “If it’s super duper loud, I put both my ears in. It’s a lot. You can get a real massive headache.” To protect her ears from both external stadium volume and high-volume broadcast feeds, Andrews opted for custom-fitted, full-mold IFB earpieces rather than standard single-ear acoustic tubes. Even then, she faces a constant tug-of-war throughout all four quarters. Of course, it isn’t just Erin Andrews who has trouble with the loud crowd. Monday Night Football sideline reporter Laura Rutledge previously expressed her worries about losing her hearing because of loud fans at Arrowhead Stadium. “It’s definitely Arrowhead. It is crazy in there,” the ESPN sideline reporter said via GMFB. “So, we have these ear pieces in our ears, and I always tell my husband, ‘I can’t hear.’ I am maybe losing my hearing because of places like Arrowhead.” Long-term exposure to loud noises above 85 decibels can actually lead to permanent ear damage, called noise-induced hearing loss (NIHL). item.title: Big blow for Real Madrid as Mikel Arteta confirms the return of Arsenal sensation
item.description: Big blow for Real Madrid as Mikel Arteta confirms the return of Arsenal sensation Real Madrid have been by far the best-performing team in the UEFA Champions League, having secured five wins in five matches so far this season. Jose Mourinho’s men firmly have one foot inside the top eight, and another win could further solidify their position as league leaders, with the coach quite happy with the current bunch . However, Real Madrid’s next game is against Premier League champions Arsenal, a daunting opposition known for their discipline and defensive solidity. Real Madrid are slated to face Arsenal on December 9, in what will be their final UCL game of the year. Arsenal handed huge boost Bukayo Saka picked up a knock against Bayern. (Photo by Leonhard Simon/Getty Images) With a couple of weeks remaining before they face Real Madrid, Arsenal have been handed a major boost. As reported by Mundo Deportivo , Arsenal coach Mikel Arteta has confirmed that Bukayo Saka has returned to training and will soon return to the pitch. Saka had picked up a hamstring injury on October 21 against Bayern Munich. He has since missed seven matches across all competitions. In Saka’s absence, Arsenal have won four matches, drawn two and have been eliminated in the Round of 16 of the League Cup against Fleetwood Town via penalties. Will Saka be fit to play against Real Madrid? Saka could cause problems for the Real Madrid defence. (Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images) The report suggests Saka will not be fit enough to play in Arsenal’s next game against Manchester City in the Premier League. However, the English international may receive a few minutes against Brentford and Tottenham Hotspur before Arsenal host Real Madrid on December 9. There is a good chance Saka will be fit to play against Los Blancos . Coach Arteta has so far relied on the services of Noni Madueke, who has struggled to provide any real quality to the table. Saka, therefore, will be a major upgrade for Arsenal. He will cause a headache for a Real Madrid defence that has largely done well, especially on the left flank, with new signing Marc Cucurella offering ample solidity. The duel between Cucurella and Saka will be an interesting one to monitor and may well decide the fate of the clash, as the Gunners look to return to winning ways in the Champions League.

item.title: Victor Wembanyama Reveals How He Plans To Win His First NBA MVP Award
item.description: Nov 21, 2026; San Antonio, Texas, USA; San Antonio Spurs forward Victor Wembanyama (1) looks over in the first half against the New Orleans Pelicans at Frost Bank Center. Mandatory Credit: Daniel Dunn-Imagn Images Victor Wembanyama thinks dominating the rim at both ends will deliver his first NBA MVP award. And his latest victory over Luka Doncic was just an example of why that approach could work. After the San Antonio Spurs rallied past the Los Angeles Lakers 99-96 on Friday, Wembanyama explained that his championship ambitions and individual goals share the same foundation: controlling the paint while creating chances for his teammates. “At the rim, dominate the rim on offense, my teammates are open, you know. This is the way we’ve won many games last year. This is the way we’re gonna win many games this year.” “I’m gonna have to take the mid-range shot, especially the late-game isos and stuff, and the threes, of course. But dominating the rim on both sides is how I’m gonna win MVP one day.” Wembanyama made these comments during his postgame interview with Prime Video , laying out an approach that combines interior dominance with the versatility needed to answer multiple defensive strategies. The season numbers have already given that MVP talk substance. Through 19 games, Wembanyama is averaging 30.4 points, 12.7 rebounds, 3.1 assists, 1.4 steals, and 3.7 blocks. He is shooting 53.4% from the field and 32.0% from three-point range. These figures just put his value in perspective. He can carry a major scoring burden, finish defensive possessions with rebounds, and erase mistakes around the basket. His influence on shot selection can also extend beyond the attempts he actually blocks. Offensively, attacking the rim can force defenders to collapse, which creates open shots for his teammates. Establishing that threat on a consistent basis gives the Spurs a great starting point, while his midrange shooting and three-point range do give him good options when opponents crowd the lane. The Lakers game showed how that broader impact can survive an inefficient scoring night. Wembanyama finished with 25 points, 16 rebounds, two assists, four steals, and two blocks despite shooting 10-of-25 from the field overall. The Spurs recovered from a 20-point deficit to improve to 16-4, while the Lakers fell to 15-4. His free-throw shooting also had a lot of room for improvement, as he made just three of his eight attempts against the Lakers. Converting those chances will make his interior aggression even more valuable and would help the Spurs protect their leads late in very tightly contested games. Luka, his main MVP rival, had 31 points, six rebounds, and eight assists, but he shot 1-of-13 from three-point range. item.title: Report: Arsenal in contact with Nico Paz sparking transfer battle with Man United
item.description: Report: Arsenal in contact with Nico Paz sparking transfer battle with Man United ESPN Argentina reports that Arsenal have been in contact with representatives of Como star Nico Paz, sparking a transfer battle with Premier League rivals Manchester United. Como star Nico Paz has attracted interest from several clubs around Europe. Nico Paz transfer latest as Arsenal and Man United linked OCTOBER 21: Nico Paz of Como 1907 celebrates scoring his team’s first goal during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 match between Como 1907 and Manchester United at Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium on October 21, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) The latest report from ESPN Argentina, quoted by AlbicelesteTalk, claims that Premier League giants Arsenal have been in contact with the Argentine’s representatives and have scouted him several times this season. According to the report, Arsenal are ready to seriously pursue the 22-year-old in the 2027 summer transfer window. ITALY – OCTOBER 21: Nico Paz of Como 1907 celebrates scoring his team’s third goal with teammates during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 match between Como 1907 and Manchester United at Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium on October 21, 2026 in Italy. item.title: Xabi Alonso issues desperate plea as Chelsea fans turn on Wesley Fofana in Nottingham Forest defeat
item.description: Liverpool v Chelsea - Carabao Cup Fourth Round - Getty Images Sport Pressure is mounting on Xabi Alonso after Chelsea suffered a third successive Premier League defeat in a 3-2 loss at Nottingham Forest on Friday night. Amid a hostile evening that saw Wesley Fofana jeered by his own supporters following a controversial interview, the Blues boss issued a rallying call to the club. Chelsea slump to third straight defeat Chelsea's miserable run in the Premier League continued on Friday night as they fell 3-2 away to Forest . The setback marked a third consecutive league loss for the Blues and piled further scrutiny on manager Alonso. Forest seized control through a stunning early volley from Igor Jesus, before Morgan Gibbs-White struck twice to steer the hosts to victory. Substitute Emmanuel Emegha netted a double for the visitors, yet his goals ultimately proved in vain. Beyond the result, the evening was overshadowed by a fractious atmosphere in the away end. Fofana found himself targeted by his own club's supporters, who jeered the defender every time he touched the ball . Alonso demands unity in the dressing room Despite the growing tension on the pitch and in the stands, Alonso immediately jumped to Fofana's defence during his post-match press conference. The Chelsea boss stressed that the entire club must remain united to weather the storm. "We have to stick together, and everyone that is in the changing room, everyone in the team is needed," Alonso said, as quoted by TNT Sports . "We need to help, and we need to go through these tough moments all together, and we don't leave anyone apart. "We need to support everyone. That is because we need everyone, and we need the fans. In the footage, the defender appeared to joke about missing his spot-kick during last month's Carabao Cup penalty shootout defeat to Liverpool. The Frenchman is said to have apologised to his team-mates for those remarks, but his night at Forest went from bad to worse when he conceded a penalty for Gibbs-White's second goal. When pressed on whether the supporters' hostile reaction would make it difficult to select Fofana moving forward, Alonso remained guarded. "Well, I'm thinking right after the game, and for the next games. We will see," he replied. item.title: “His Career Is Over”: Ryan Fitzpatrick Calls Out Aaron Rodgers For Seemingly Backtracking on Keyser Söze Plan
item.description: Aaron Rodgers. © Imagn Aaron Rodgers has found himself at the center of another NFL controversy over how he handled his situation with Mike McCarthy. Rodgers was released by the Pittsburgh Steelers after his explosive comments about McCarthy on The Pat McAfee Show. The quarterback accused his former coach of falling asleep during meetings and questioned his approach to managing the team. Former NFL quarterback Ryan Fitzpatrick addressed what comes next for Rodgers. Speaking on NFL on Prime Video, Fitzpatrick questioned why the quarterback felt the need to air his grievances in public. “I just think it’s fascinating because all we’ve heard from Aaron is the Keyser Söze thing. Once his career is over, we’re never going to see him again. He’s not going to live a public life. He’s not going to be on TV. He’s not going to do any appearances. And yet we’re one day into this, and he has to make sure that he has the final word and he writes the narrative. “…I would be shocked if he went to go play for another team this year, which means that his career is over,” Fitzpatrick said. Fitzpatrick’s comments came after Rodgers sent a text message to Al Michaels during the Steelers-Broncos Black Friday broadcast defending his decision to speak publicly about the McCarthy situation after being criticized by Tom Brady. “The code or sanctity exists to protect the integrity of the locker room, not to provide immunity from accountability for its leadership. They took this to the public. Never heard from the head coach. Then they leaked at 11 p.m. They also barred me from the facility. That’s why I went to McAfee,” Michaels quoted Rodgers as saying. The Keyser Söze reference was to comments Rodgers made in 2025, when he said he wanted to step away from the spotlight after retiring. “I don’t want the attention – I know that’s a narrative out there. When this is all done, it’s Keyser Söze. You won’t see me. I won’t be in the public. I don’t want to live a public life,” Rodgers said on The Pat McAfee Show, per NBC Sports . Will Aaron Rodgers Return for Another Year? Aaron Rodgers had previously indicated that the current season would be his final one in the NFL. In July, a reporter asked Rodgers if this would be his last season. “Yeah, this is it. … I thought last year might be it, but then Mike McCarthy got hired and I talked to my wife and she said, ‘You can do one more year,'” he said, per Brendan Howe. “No, zero debate,” he added when asked if this was his final decision. For now, Rodgers’ NFL future remains uncertain. He cleared waivers on Thursday and is now a free agent. item.title: Cristobal Gets Critical Boost As Ja’Boree Antoine Returns
item.description: Credit: Bob Donnan-Imagn Images The Miami Hurricanes are set to welcome back a key piece of their secondary just as the season hits its most critical stretch. Saturday’s matchup against Boston College should mark Ja’Boree Antoine’s season debut, concluding a prolonged period of anticipation for both the fanbase and the coaching staff. EssentiallySports reports that the secondary has spent the entire season patching holes by moving safeties to cornerback just to remain competitive. That kind of makeshift lineup rarely works against top-tier competition. A setback in August derailed his plans to become a key defensive component. Now, he is back on the field and ready to help stop the run and cover receivers. According to EssentiallySports, Antoine joined the program in Coral Gables as a top-200 national prospect and a blue-chip four-star recruit in the 2025 class. The 6-foot-1, 180-pound sophomore appeared in 12 games last season and was anticipated to assume a larger role. He showed he could handle that load with seven combined tackles and one pass breakup in 2025. Before the injury occurred, the coaching staff had observed enough potential to anticipate a significant second-year improvement from him. A fall camp injury put those plans on hold, but the recovery is ahead of schedule. Antoine had already resumed on-field practice in cleats during the week preceding Miami’s game with Virginia Tech. Yahoo Sports indicates that his return is near enough for the coaching staff to contemplate deploying him against Boston College. As reported by EssentiallySports, Miami is entering the most critical phase of its season. The defense has struggled to find consistency without its top talent. Bringing him back gives the unit a level of speed and coverage it has lacked for weeks. The staff knows this is the right time to get him back on the field. The road ahead is tough, but the roster looks stronger than it did a month ago.

item.description: ‘You May Not Agree With Aaron Rodgers’ — Patrick Mahomes’ Trainer Highlights Steelers’ ‘Positive Change’ After QB’s Release, Mike McCarthy Controversy The Pittsburgh Steelers may have found a fresh start after parting ways with Aaron Rodgers. Following a turbulent week involving the veteran quarterback and head coach Mike McCarthy, Pittsburgh delivered a convincing 27-5 win over the Denver Broncos on Black Friday. The performance caught the attention of Patrick Mahomes’ longtime trainer, Bobby Stroupe, who believes a positive change has already taken root in Pittsburgh. Bobby Stroupe Reacts to Steelers’ Remarkable Turnaround Stroupe took to X after the Steelers’ victory to share his thoughts on Rodgers’ departure and its impact on the team. “You may not agree with Aaron Rodgers and how he went about it, but I promise you that positive change has taken place. So there is that,” Stroupe wrote. On the field, that shift was immediately visible. Making his first start after Rodgers’ benching, Mason Rudolph was a steady hand, throwing for 142 yards and a touchdown without committing a turnover. His 77.5 PFN QB Impact Grade is third in the league this week through Black Friday. Pittsburgh’s defense was even more impressive. T.J. Watt recovered a fumble for a touchdown, while Jalen Ramsey added a pick-six to help the Steelers secure a 22-point victory. item.description: Republic of Ireland are aiming to reach a second successive World Cup [Getty Images] The Republic of Ireland are potentially just 180 minutes away from booking their spot at consecutive Women's World Cups. Standing in their way to next year's tournament are familiar foes in the form of Poland, who they beat twice in their qualifying group. They will play the Poles twice more, with the first leg in Gdansk on Tuesday, 1 December and the second leg at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin on Saturday, 5 December with the winner securing their place on the plane to Brazil. Ahead of a potentially defining week for Carla Ward and her players, BBC Sport NI looks at how they are gearing up for the massive play-off games. Republic of Ireland boss Ward signs new contract Mustaki out of World Cup play-off with knee injury Ward's new deal overshadowed by Mustaki's injury Mustaki ruptured her ACL while playing for Nottingham Forest against Liverpool [Getty Images] It's been a mix of good and bad news for Republic of Ireland in the build-up to the two games. There was the welcome announcement on Monday that head coach Ward had signed a new contract until the end of the Euro 2029 campaign. Ward's current deal was set to expire at the end of this World Cup qualification campaign and it will be a relief to the manager and players that she that will stay, irrespective of how the play-off pans out. It offers stability that the Irish have lacked in recent years and it is certainly well deserved given she has overseen 12 victories in her 19 games, including promotion to League A and excellent performances in their group against the Poles, France and Netherlands. Ward's legacy will really be enhanced if she can follow Vera Pauw in leading the team to another World Cup and she can fully focus on doing so now that her future has been resolved before this window. That announcement had followed the devastating blow that Ward had been dealt earlier on Monday, the confirmation that defender Chloe Mustaki would miss the play-off with a knee injury. Mustaki, who has been integral for the Irish as a left-sided centre-back under Ward, ruptured her anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) in action for Nottingham Forest against Liverpool in the League Cup last week. Ward said it was "a really difficult setback" for Mustaki, who also suffered an ACL injury in 2020 and was diagnosed with Hodgkin's lymphoma aged 19. Her club announced that she would miss the rest of the season and she would also likely have to sit out the World Cup if the Irish do qualify. Ward did not call up a replacement to her 24-strong squad that gathered in Dublin on Tuesday and with everyone else fully fit, she will hope they have enough to get over the line even without Mustaki. After watching him bowl a couple of overs, Wright, then part of the Mumbai Indians support staff, approached Gujarat captain Parthiv Patel and asked: "Who's that bloke there?" The trademark short, stuttering run-up, unusual delivery stride and slingy release make him unlike almost every other fast bowler. item.description: SPORTS-BKC-STORY-COLUMN-FILEPIC-LX Kentucky head coach Mark Pope reacts during the Wildcats 90-76 loss against Indiana at Lucas Oil Stadium on Nov. 20, 2026, in Indianapolis. Ryan C. Hermens/Lexington Herald-Leader/TNS EDITORIAL USE ONLY Copyright: xLexingtonxHerald-Leaderx 190657633W RyanxC.xHermensx krtphotoslive968862 ©IMAGO/Newscom World Mark Pope is not looking for anyone else to blame after Kentucky’s embarrassing overtime defeat to Wichita State. The Wildcats had one final opportunity to steal a win at Rupp Arena, but a costly mistake on the baseline with only five seconds left left them with virtually no chance of doing that. And as Pope made clear after the game, the blame rests entirely on his shoulders. “That’s 100% on me, guys. That is 100% me. Somehow that changed to a live ball in my mind, and I messed that up. It was really costly. It’s a tough one to carry as a coach for sure,” Pope said during the postgame press conference shared on the Kentucky radio YouTube channel. Trailing 73–71 in overtime at Rupp Arena, Kentucky forced a turnover when a Wichita State pass went out of bounds under the basket with roughly five seconds left. Following a timeout, Pope drew up a play where inbounder Alex Wilkins passed the ball along the baseline to teammate Mason Williams, who was standing out of bounds. However, under NCAA rules, a player can only run the baseline and pass to a teammate standing out of bounds following a made basket, not after a dead-ball turnover. As a result, officials immediately whistled Kentucky for an illegal inbounds pass and awarded possession back to Wichita State. When a coach takes full responsibility for a costly mistake, it reveals character. Stay updated on Kentucky basketball's response and what's next for Mark Pope's squad. Although Kentucky managed to steal Wichita State’s subsequent long inbound pass, Milan Momcilovic’s open three-pointer at the buzzer rimmed out. That left the score at 73–71, sealing the victory for the Wichita State Shockers. When pressed on whether any assistant coaches or players in the huddle realized the play was illegal before the whistle, Pope refused to share the blame. “That is me. It’s 100% me. Don’t try and spread that to anyone else. That is 100% me. That’s on my shoulders,” he stated. The loss dropped Kentucky to 4-3 on the season after the Wildcats blew a 14-point lead and were heavily outrebounded (55 to 36) without center Malachi Moreno , who missed the game while in concussion protocol. The defeat, which also occurred during a night celebrating the 50th anniversary of Rupp Arena, sparked loud boos from the home crowd as the team exited the floor and intensified scrutiny on Pope’s third season in Lexington. The Wildcats have now lost two consecutive games and will be hoping to bounce back when they face the unbeaten No. 2 Virginia Cavaliers in their next game on Wednesday, December 2. item.title: What does Sean Steur think of all this?
item.description: Sean Steur Declan Rice Sean Steur was the stand out Newcastle United signing of summer 2026. I don’t think there is any debate otherwise. When Sean Steur left the pitch against Arsenal last weekend it was a vocal minority of Newcastle United fans booing. A largely young and inexperienced Newcastle United team and squad, that lost so many of its best players, that is struggling for confidence and consistency, then getting booed time and time again. Is that really going to help them??? I also wonder what Sean Steur is thinking when he sees how the likes of Bruno Guimaraes was treated last weekend by so many of the Newcastle United fans . I think booing on that occasion to try and put Bruno off was fair enough BUT it felt like it went far beyond that. Hatred for many? It feels like any player who chooses to leave, is now fair game to get this abuse, no matter what they have done for Newcastle United. What does Sean Steur think when he sees and hears that? item.title: Lazio & Roma Keen to Bring Former Inter Milan Defender Back to Serie A
item.description: Lazio & Roma Keen to Bring Former Inter Milan Defender Back to Serie A Lazio and Roma are reportedly interested in Olympiacos centre-back Lorenzo Pirola, who would relish the opportunity to return to Italy. Lorenzo Pirola: From Inter Milan to Olympiacos The 24-year-old is an Inter Milan youth product who has only played 10 minutes for the Nerazzurri at the senior level. Between 2020 and 2022, the defender was on loan at Monza, and he then spent the 2022/23 campaign at Salernitana, who exercised the option to buy him, before selling him to Olympiacos in the summer of 2024. Pirola’s Greek Exploits Lirola has now established himself as a stalwart at the back for the Greek giants. He has already made 82 appearances for the club, scoring a goal and providing an assist. But with his contract expiring in June 2028, a long-term future in Athens remains far from guaranteed. Lazio & Roma Could Duel for Pirola According to Tuttosport (via La Lazio Siamo Noi ), contract renewal talks between Pirola and Olympiacos are currently on hold. This could pave the way for an exit, either in January or in the summer, as the Greek side wouldn’t want to risk losing the player for free a year later. Gattuso Rules Out Lazio Formation Change Against Torino, Provides Injury Updates The Turin-based newspaper believes a return to Serie A would be the most plausible solution for the Inter academy product, identifying Roma and Lazio as his main suitors. Lazio Could Use Their Rapport with Pirola’s Agent As the source explains, the Giallorossi have been tracking the player for quite some time, while the Biancocelesti have an excellent rapport with his agent Beppe Riso, who also represents Nicolo Rovella, Davide Frattesi, and Andrea Pinamonti. Why Lazio Won’t Sign Pirola in January At this stage, we can confidently rule out Pirola’s arrival at Lazio in January. First, the club seriously risks another transfer ban due to their unbalanced financial accounts. Second, Gennaro Gattuso already has four competent centre-backs at his disposal, including two left-footed in the form of Oliver Provstgaard and Diogo Leite. Therefore, this move would only be viable in the summer.

item.title: Niclas Füllkrug challenges Werder Bremen to meet higher standards after 3-3 Bundesliga draw
item.description: Niclas Füllkrug challenges Werder Bremen to meet higher standards after 3-3 Bundesliga draw Werder Bremen striker Niclas Füllkrug was far from satisfied with his team’s performance despite rescuing a point in Friday evening’s dramatic 3-3 Bundesliga draw against Borussia Mönchengladbach . The 33-year-old Germany international scored an acrobatic stoppage-time equalizer but criticized Bremen’s wastefulness and poor passing throughout the encounter. Füllkrug’s 11th Bundesliga goal of the season helped Daniel Thioune’s side recover from a 3-1 deficit. The Bundesliga’s leading goal-scorer nevertheless felt that Bremen had fallen well short of the standards established during their impressive start to the campaign. “When you play the way we have so far, your own expectations rise,” Füllkrug – as quoted by Kicker – said after the match. “Of course I’m disappointed. We were far too sloppy and lost possession far too often. Our mentality was excellent, but we still need to play clean football, bring our quality onto the pitch, and know exactly where we need to improve. We fell short in that respect today. We have to be honest about that.” Niclas Füllkrug identifies tactical shortcomings and reflects on possible dismissal The veteran striker was particularly frustrated by Bremen’s inability to exploit passing opportunities in central midfield. “Our No. 6 was often free, but we simply couldn’t find him,” Füllkrug explained. “We could have switched play or played forward into space. Instead, everything required an enormous amount of effort. That annoys me. We had clear-cut chances in the second half. You could see that the final bit of conviction was missing, not because we didn’t have it, but because the effort was so great. You’re constantly pressing at such high intensity to win the ball, and then suddenly you’re through on goal and missing that final bit of focus.” The striker was fortunate to remain on the pitch after catching Kevin Diks on the ankle in the 60th minute. Already booked following an earlier confrontation with Philipp Sander, Füllkrug avoided a second caution from referee Felix Zwayer. “Was that a yellow?” Füllkrug asked after reviewing the incident on television. “I was trying to play the ball with the tip of my boot. I don’t know whether that’s a yellow card. No idea. That’s for the referee to decide.” GGFN | Peter Weis

item.title: "Now we need to show what sort of team we are" – Bischof on injury-depleted Bayern
item.description: "Now we need to show what sort of team we are" – Bischof on injury-depleted Bayern Bayern Munich find themselves in an unusual position early in the season. The Bavarians are second in the Bundesliga, trailing Borussia Dortmund by two points. The Champions League has also seen mixed results, with Bayern winning only one of their last four matches. Significant injuries have pushed youngsters to the forefront. Among those is midfielder Tom Bischof, who has become a key player in his second season with the club. He's started Bayern's last four Champions League matches and is making the most of the opportunity. “Being at it every day and week is really important,” said Bischof in an interview with the DFL. "I got the experience of playing three or four games in a row because others were out, so you always have to be there.” Bayern have faced a brutal injury stretch, most recently when Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane got hurt in a 1-1 draw with 1. FC Köln. The English striker is expected to be sidelined for around three months. "We had a chat with him at half-time, and he already felt it could be a bad one," Bischof said. “So we were already thinking about things then.” The response from the club has been underwhelming so far. Vincent Kompany was forced into an improvised starting eleven against Lille without Kane, Luis Diaz, Michael Olise, and Jamal Musiala, among others. Bischof started and recorded an assist, but Bayern still fell 2-1. The Lille result marked the club's first loss in all competitions since last April against PSG. Additionally, the Köln draw, combined with Borussia Dortmund recording three points against Borussia Mönchengladbach, saw Kompany's side slide to second in the Bundesliga. Niko Kovač's Dortmund have emerged as legitimate title contenders. “Dortmund are in good form and picking up hard points,” Bischof said. “We’ve had one or two draws that we maybe shouldn’t have had, but hopefully we get there in the end." For Bischof, seeing Bayern struggle is almost an entirely new concept. Last season, Bayern won the Bundesliga with 89 points, finishing 16 clear of Dortmund. Kompany's side lost only one league match. There was never a title race. This year is clearly different, but Bischof doesn't expect the increased pressure from Dortmund to change Bayern's mentality. “I think we saw last season that, even though things weren’t as tight as they are at the moment this year, we still didn’t let up," Bischof said. “I’ve never seen us lack motivation or to let up. We always go full throttle for every game.” The club has six games left to close out 2026, with four in the Bundesliga and matches in the DFB Pokal as well as the Champions League. Bischof and Bayern must end the year on a high, and that expectation is nothing new. “Now we need to show what sort of team we are,” Bischof said. “I think we’ve shown that often enough.”

item.description: Alexander Zverev. © Reuters Alexander Zverev has issued a defiant response to the relentless criticism of his World No. 1 status and his two Grand Slam title triumphs in 2026. Most of the German’s fans came out in support, furiously urging critics to stop taking swipes at him. Much of the criticism stems from the fact that Zverev reached the No. 1 ranking in a year when rivals Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner were absent for long periods due to injuries. He also did not have to face either of them in his title-winning runs in Roland Garros and New York. In the aftermath of Germany’s exit from the 2026 Davis Cup Finals in the quarterfinals, Zverev hit back at critics, saying: “All these debates about my ranking position are made by people who have never played tennis. It’s very simple: there’s a pool of points over 12 months, and whoever earns the most points is No. 1.” Going on to proudly speak about his performances and results spanning the four Majors in 2026, Zverev added: “This year, I want to point out that across the four Slams, my worst result was the semifinals at the Australian Open—then I made a final and won two Slams. I deserve to be No. 1.” Several fans of Zverev on X (formerly Twitter) vociferously defended the German. One fan wrote: (translated from Italian by Grok) “Again? Come on, leave him alone!” Another added: “You really should not have to keep justifying yourself! It’s so wrong! You deserve everything you’ve achieved!” “Alexander Zverev really deserves the World No. 1 ranking” – Carlos Alcaraz after defeating the German in the championship match at the 2026 ATP Finals Zverev’s No. 1 credentials came under further scrutiny after Alcaraz thoroughly outplayed him in the championship match at the 2026 ATP Finals in Turin. However, during his post-match press conference, Alcaraz himself acknowledged his German rival’s ascent to the summit of the rankings. The former No. 1 and career Grand Slam champion told reporters: “The No. 1 is Sascha (Zverev’s nickname). He really deserves it. Nobody’s going to take that position and the No. 1 away from him. We have to think about it. We have to say that. Right now, the ranking says it’s Sascha, and we have to give credit to him.” It’s worth noting that in his head-to-head against Alcaraz and Sinner, Zverev has a losing record. Against Alcaraz, the German star has played 14 matches and lost 8; against Sinner, Zverev has clashed 15 times and lost 11. item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. However, general manager Will Kuntz , speaking in a videoconference with the media Friday, agreed things are dismal. “I don’t think we did a good enough job collectively last year,” he said. “So for us, it’s really about taking a hard look at everything we’ve done process-wise and saying ‘hey, how can we be better?’ Because it cannot continue like this.” Galaxy coach Greg Vanney reacts during a match against LAFC at BMO Stadium on Oct. 25. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram.
